linear.text: Claim under test: Dissociation unlocks catalase-like activity: only dissociated MVs consume H2O2 and evolve O2
Read the panel: F1n [ASSAY]
Ruling: Residual H2O2 after each repeated H2O2 spike rises from 28 to 38 to 40 uM

traces.question: The claim under test is offered as read off panel F1n. Based only on what that panel actually shows for residual H2O2 across the repeated H2O2 spikes, does the panel support the claim as stated?
traces.answer_key: No, not straightforwardly. Panel F1n shows residual H2O2 after each repeated H2O2 spike rising from 28 to 38 to 40 uM (a3) -- the unconsumed H2O2 accumulates across successive spikes rather than being fully consumed, so the plot itself does not simply confirm the claim; the text asserts consumption but the ruling has to come from this rising residual series.
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, i.e., the content of node a3 (the read_trend verdict on panel F1n) as the sole graded target.

linear.text: Claim under test: In 4T1 tumours Dox-MVs raise sO2 from 2.7% to 17.5% at 24 h and cut the HIF-1a-positive area to 7%
Read the panel: F3e [CT]
Ruling: Tumour sO2 with Dox-MVs falls back to 8.8% at 48 h, half its 24 h value

traces.question: The claim under test states that Dox-MVs raise tumour sO2 from 2.7% to 17.5% at the 24 h timepoint. Looking at panel F3e, which plots tumour sO2 over time for the PBS, Dox and Dox-MVs groups, what does the Dox-MVs trace show for the sO2 level once the timepoint moves past 24 h to 48 h?
traces.answer_key: The panel shows that tumour sO2 in the Dox-MVs group does not stay at its 24 h level: it falls back to 8.8% at 48 h, which is half of its 24 h value.
